evals.prompt: Plan and orchestrate a comprehensive multi-phase refactoring campaign for a 25k-LOC legacy Python 3.10 service that has Bandit findings, 42% test coverage, dead modules, grade-E `radon` functions, and `setup.py` packaging.
evals.expected_output: An impact-ordered orchestration plan capturing baseline metrics in `reports/` first, then executing phases strictly in safety order: (1) `py-security` (remediate vulnerabilities first), (2) `py-test-quality` (raise branch coverage >= 80% and mutation score >= 75% BEFORE structural refactoring), (3) `py-code-health` (delete dead/duplicate code so we don't refactor unused code), (4) `py-complexity` (decompose complex functions under the test safety net), (5) `py-modernize` + `py-quality-setup` + `py-git-hooks` (lock gains in CI/pre-commit).
expectations: Captures baseline security, coverage, dead-code, and complexity metrics into `reports/` before modifying production code
Orders phases strictly as Security -> Test Quality -> Code Health -> Complexity -> Modernization / Quality Gates
Explains why `py-test-quality` (>= 80% coverage / >= 75% mutation score) MUST run before `py-code-health` and `py-complexity` structural changes
Requires atomic per-phase commits with green test/linter gates between phases and final before/after metric comparison

evals.prompt: A teammate wants to kick off a full `py-refactor` campaign right now during an active P1 checkout outage, and also asks whether to run the full 5-phase campaign on a brand-new module that has zero tests and a single SQL injection bug.
evals.expected_output: Applies `py-refactor`'s explicit scope and safety boundaries: refuses full multi-phase refactoring during an active production incident (stabilize the P1 incident with minimal surgical hotfix first), notes that a single isolated vulnerability belongs directly to `py-security` rather than full orchestration, and requires establishing a `py-test-quality` safety net on zero-test modules before any complexity or dead-code refactoring.
expectations: Advises against running a broad refactoring campaign during an active P1 production outage
Routes a narrow single-vulnerability fix directly to `py-security` rather than over-orchestrating all five phases
Refuses structural/complexity refactoring on zero-test modules until `py-test-quality` establishes characterization/unit tests
Specifies clear entry criteria and rollback checkpoints per phase

evals.prompt: We finished Phases 1–4 of a Python refactoring initiative (`py-security`, `py-test-quality`, `py-code-health`, `py-complexity`). Show how to verify measurable improvement against baseline and lock the repository against regression.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs the exact baseline commands (`ruff check --select S` / `bandit`, `pytest --cov --cov-branch`, `mutmut results`, `vulture`, `radon cc` / `radon mi` / `wily diff`) to produce a before/after delta report in `reports/`, then applies `py-modernize`, `py-quality-setup`, and `py-git-hooks` so pre-commit and CI enforce zero backsliding.
expectations: Re-runs security, branch coverage, mutation score, dead-code, and `radon`/`wily` complexity metrics and compares them against the saved baseline in `reports/`
Executes `py-modernize` (`uv`, Python 3.13 syntax) only after dead code and high-complexity blocks have already been cleaned up
Verifies the full test suite and typecheckers pass cleanly before closing the refactoring campaign
